title: Label legacy task verification as agent-reported
description:
Compatibility slice of the human-confirmed CheckRun decomposition. Objective: distinguish an agent's existing complete_task verification claim from runner-reported candidate-bound CheckRun evidence without changing whether legacy projects can complete work.

Deliverable in exactly five owned paths: packages/moe-daemon/src/types/schema.ts extends TaskVerification with optional source:'agent-reported' (optional for old records); tools/completeTask.ts persists that literal after normal validation; tools/getContext.ts projects the literal on both primary task.verification and declared-prerequisite verification; tools/completeTask.test.ts and tools/getContext.test.ts prove the real production writer/readers. Existing missing verification remains null. Existing reports without a source are projected as agent-reported without a read-time disk write. Do not let an imported/manual/caller-provided source label elevate a TaskVerification to runner-observed. The main task's verification projection preserves command/exitCode/outputTail/reportedAt, while the compact prerequisite projection still omits outputTail.

Use existing util/enforcement.ts assertVerificationEvidence UNCHANGED: required evidence, nonzero refusal, command trimming, 500-character command cap and final 2000-character output tail all retain their old semantics. complete_task keeps ownership/step/branch/error precedence and its REVIEW/finalizing transition. Place source:'agent-reported' AFTER spreads so it cannot be overridden, and do not add source to the accepted complete_task verification input schema. No candidate id exists for this legacy path; never synthesize a Candidate or write a fake bound CheckRun. Store the label in the existing task.verification object and expose it there, including when no attempt/candidate/checks directory exists, autoCommit=false or there is no Git repository.

Depends on the store slice ONLY to serialize the shared schema.ts edit and its preceding QA-binding schema/getContext work. The original task-867f69a6 remains the complete recorder DoD gate and will document this behavior in docs/MCP_SERVER.md. NOT in scope: CheckRun store/tool/registry, new commands, verification validation/refusal changes, source authentication, policy/QA/dependency gates, migrations, IDE/wrapper edits, or held-out acceptance-test edits/unskips.

Verification at repo root Windows: cmd /d /c "cd /d packages\moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/tools/completeTask.test.ts src/tools/getContext.test.ts && npm test && npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json". macOS/Linux: (cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/tools/completeTask.test.ts src/tools/getContext.test.ts && npm test && npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json). Require nonzero counts and exact old-writer/read behavior assertion red, not a compile failure. Do not run build/prebuild/clean or discard peer state.

Real get_context exposes agent-reported for both the primary task and declared-prerequisite projections of legacy source-less records without rewriting their files; null/missing verification remains null and sibling outputTail remains omitted.
Tests prove attempted caller or persisted-label promotion cannot produce runner-observed TaskVerification, and no Candidate/CheckRun/runner identity is fabricated.
Existing verification validation/refusal behavior and complete_task REVIEW/finalizing transitions remain unchanged, with no edits to util/enforcement.ts or held-out tests.
Tests cover legacy no-attempt/no-candidate/no-git and autoCommit=false completion paths plus compact sibling projection, preserving existing fields and failures.
Named focused tests, npm test and tsc all exit 0 with nonzero executed counts; an assertion regression fails against the old source-less writer/readers, and only the five owned files change.

Do not weaken or reimplement assertVerificationEvidence, change its input shape or apply the new CheckRun byte cap to legacy outputTail.
Preserve landed QA candidate-binding behavior and all foreign hunks when editing getContext/schema.
No policy gate or held-out-test unskip belongs to this compatibility slice.
